title: Review: Combustion and fuels; Formulae and functional groups; Homologous series
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR01#t1 term and clue written for the game; OR01#t2 term and clue written for the game; EN11#t1 term and clue written for the game; EN11#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EN11#N.14, OR01#N.5, OR02#N.4, EN11#N.3, OR01#N.9, OR02#N.7, EN11#N.8, OR01#N.11, OR02#N.9, EN11#N.5, EN11#N.15. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Skeletal formula
items.clue: A zig-zag of C–C bonds in which H on carbon is left out.

items.label: Displayed formula
items.clue: A drawing that shows every atom and every bond, including O–H.

items.label: Complete combustion
items.clue: Burning in plenty of O₂, so that all C ends as CO₂ and all H as H₂O.

items.label: Carbon monoxide
items.clue: Colourless, odourless, toxic gas formed when a fuel burns in limited oxygen.

questions.stem: Bioethanol is made by fermenting sugar from sugar cane and is burned as a fuel for vehicles. Which statement about bioethanol as a fuel is correct?

options.text: It burns to form water only, so using it as a fuel adds no CO₂ to the atmosphere.
The CO₂ it releases is exactly balanced by photosynthesis, so its net emission is zero.
All of its carbon was fixed from atmospheric CO₂ by photosynthesis in the cane.
Its carbon was taken from the soil by the roots of the cane, not from CO₂ in the air.

questions.explanation: The cane took its carbon from the air within the last year or two. Even so, fossil fuels used to grow and process it add CO₂, so it is not carbon neutral.

questions.stem: Propan-2-ol has the molecular formula C₃H₈O. Which statement about the formula C₃H₈O is correct?

options.text: It is the molecular formula only, since an empirical formula is simpler.
It is a structural formula, as it lists every atom present.
It identifies propan-2-ol, since no other compound has this formula.
It is both the molecular and the empirical formula of propan-2-ol.

questions.explanation: 3, 8 and 1 have no common factor, so the ratio is already the simplest. Empirical = molecular here.

questions.stem: Which pair of compounds are successive members of the same homologous series?

options.text: CH₃CH₂CHO and CH₃COCH₂CH₃
CH₃COOH and CH₃CH₂COOH
CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl and CH₃CHClCH₃
CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ and CH₃CH=CHCH₃

questions.explanation: Both are carboxylic acids (CₙH₂ₙO₂) and they differ by one CH₂: ethanoic acid and propanoic acid.

questions.stem: When the equation for the complete combustion of octane, C₈H₁₈, is balanced with a coefficient of 2 for octane, what is the coefficient of O₂?
questions.explanation: 2C₈H₁₈ forms 16CO₂ and 18H₂O, which contain 16 × 2 + 18 = 50 O atoms. Each O₂ supplies two O atoms, so 25 O₂ are needed.

questions.stem: Which compound contains an ester group?

options.text: CH₃COOH
CH₃CH₂OCH₃
CH₃COOCH₃
CH₃COCH₂CH₃

questions.explanation: The C=O carbon is bonded to an O that is bonded to a carbon: –COO–. This is methyl ethanoate, an ester.

questions.stem: The boiling points of four successive alcohols are: methanol 65 °C, ethanol 78 °C, propan-1-ol 97 °C and butan-1-ol 118 °C. Which statement explains this trend?

options.text: Longer molecules have more H atoms, so they form more hydrogen bonds.
Longer molecules contain more covalent bonds to break on boiling.
Heavier molecules need more energy to move, whatever the forces.
Induced dipole–dipole forces grow with chain length; each has one –OH.

questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding per molecule stays about the same. Each extra CH₂ adds electrons and contact area, so the induced dipole–dipole forces grow.

questions.stem: Which equation represents an incomplete combustion of ethanol?

options.text: C₂H₅OH(l) + 3O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 3H₂O(l)
C₂H₅OH(l) + 1½O₂(g) → 2C(s) + 3H₂O(l)
C₂H₅OH(l) + 4O(g) → 2CO(g) + 3H₂O(l)
C₂H₅OH(l) + O₂(g) → 2C(s) + 3H₂O(l)

questions.explanation: In very limited O₂ the carbon is deposited as soot while the hydrogen still forms water. 3 O atoms in the products: 1 from ethanol, 2 from O₂.

questions.stem: Two bottles both contain a liquid with the molecular formula C₂H₄O₂. Liquid X boils at 118 °C and turns blue litmus red. Liquid Y boils at 32 °C and is neutral. Which explains this?

options.text: X and Y must be the same compound, so one of the two samples must be impure.
X's molecules are heavier, so more energy is needed to separate them.
X is CH₃COOH, with a carboxyl group; Y is HCOOCH₃, with an ester group.
X is CH₃COOH, a carboxylic acid; Y is CH₃CHO, an aldehyde with no acidic O–H group.

questions.explanation: Same atoms, different structures. X's carboxyl O–H makes it acidic and lets its molecules hydrogen-bond, so it boils far higher. The ester has no O–H.

questions.stem: Butane, C₄H₁₀, boils at −1 °C and is sold as camping gas. Dodecane, C₁₂H₂₆, boils at 216 °C and is a liquid in diesel fuel. Which explains the difference?

options.text: Dodecane molecules contain more C–C and C–H bonds, which must break before it can boil.
Dodecane molecules contain more hydrogen atoms, so they form more hydrogen bonds.
Butane and dodecane belong to different homologous series, so their properties differ.
Dodecane chains are longer, so the induced dipole–dipole forces are stronger.

questions.explanation: Longer chains have more electrons and more contact, so the forces between molecules are stronger. More energy is needed to separate them.

questions.stem: What amount of oxygen, O₂, is needed to burn 0.500 mol of propan-1-ol, C₃H₇OH, completely?

options.text: 2.25 mol
2.50 mol
4.50 mol
1.25 mol

questions.explanation: C₃H₇OH + 4½O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. The products contain 10 O atoms; the alcohol supplies 1, so O₂ supplies 9: 4½ O₂ per mole. 0.500 × 4.5 = 2.25 mol.

questions.stem: After cooking outdoors, campers carry a still-glowing charcoal barbecue into their closed tent for warmth. Charcoal is almost pure carbon. Why is this deadly, even though there is no flame?

options.text: The charcoal burns to extra carbon dioxide, C + O₂ → CO₂, which binds to haemoglobin in place of oxygen.
With limited oxygen, carbon burns to carbon monoxide, 2C + O₂ → 2CO, an acidic gas that damages the lungs.
With limited oxygen, carbon burns to carbon monoxide, 2C + O₂ → 2CO, which binds to haemoglobin.
The charcoal uses up all of the oxygen in the tent, and this lack of oxygen suffocates the campers.
